newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel threatens to respond to Hizbollah attacks.
newsitem.headline: Israel threatens to respond to Hizbollah attacks.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned Lebanese guerrillas firing rockets at northern Israel on Tuesday that his country would retaliate for attacks on civilian lives.

"The prime minister said Israel will respond severely to attacks on civilian lives, and Israel hopes this message will be absorbed on the other side in all of its meaning," a statement by Netanyahu's spokesman said.

Iranian-backed Hizbollah guerrillas fired scores of Katyusha rockets into the Israeli Galilee early on Tuesday, wounding one civilian and causing some damage, witnesses said. The attack occurred a day after violence in Lebanon, some of it involving pro-Israeli militia, killed at least 10 civilians.
Israeli troops, bracing for another possible rocket barrage, ordered residents along Israel's border into shelters about 45 minutes after Katyushas fell. Hospitals went on emergency alert.

The statement from Netanyahu's office began by saying the Israeli leader saw the immediate assignment as stopping a "circle of deterioration" which he said "doesn't serve the interests of either side".
Israel wanted quiet on both sides of the border "so that the citizens of Israel and Lebanon both will be able to lead their lives in tranquility," the statement said.
